Data observed at an analysis cutoff

Source: R/CutoffData.R
CutoffData.Rd

Restricts data generated by rOncoEndpoints to patients enrolled before an analysis cutoff (calendar time) and censors PFS and OS at the cutoff. A response counts as observed when the patient responded and the response was determined before the cutoff, before dropout and before the censoring of PFS.

Usage

CutoffData(data, cutoff)

Arguments

data

A data frame returned by rOncoEndpoints.

cutoff

Calendar time of the cutoff: a scalar, or one value per simulated trial in data, in increasing order of sim (as returned by EventTime). NA means no cutoff.

Value

The rows of data with accrual_time < cutoff, with pfs_tte, pfs_event, os_tte, os_event, pfs_calendar_time and os_calendar_time recomputed, and the added columns response_obs, response_eval and cutoff.

Details

The time at which a response is determined is the time to response when it was generated (resp.timing = "ttr" in OncoArm), the landmark resp.tau, the time of the first tumor assessment, with resp.timing = "landmark", and the time of randomization with resp.timing = "none", so that the response of every enrolled patient is then observed. Patients without an observed response have response_obs = 0, as in an intention-to-treat analysis in which patients without an assessment count as non-responders. response_eval indicates whether the patient was followed up to the first tumor assessment resp.tau (NA when resp.tau is 0), for analyses restricted to patients with an assessment.

For groups without an endpoint, its columns remain NA.

Data generated by version 0.2.0 of the package have no columns resp_tau and pfs_cens_time; they are treated as having no landmark and no censoring of PFS.

Examples

arm <- OncoArm(pfs.median = 6, orr = 0.3, resp.cor = 0.4, death.prop = 0.15,
               os.median = 15, resp.timing = "ttr", resp.tau = 1.5,
               ttr.median = 2.5)
dat <- rOncoEndpoints(nsim = 2, n = 100, arms = arm, a.time = c(0, 12),
                      seed = 1)
cut <- CutoffData(dat, cutoff = 9)
table(cut$sim, cut$response_obs)
#>    
#>      0  1
#>   1 60 13
#>   2 63 19
